subject: SLO window sizing & streaming hedges — post-demo alignment
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@auroraanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: SLO window sizing & streaming hedges — post-demo alignment

Alex — thanks for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist to qualify performance and SLOs before we move to a canary.

Key takeaways from the call
- Primary SLO targets you mentioned: p95 latency goal for synchronous generation and non-streaming paths in the 150–250 ms range for typical queries; for streaming we should optimize time-to-first-token (p50) to <150 ms.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~120 req/s; expected concurrency: ~40 active sessions; short bursts up to ~400 req/s for onboarding events.
- Typical context needs: most calls are 3k–6k input tokens, but you warned about episodic spikes to ~10k tokens for batch uploads; output ranges usually 512–2k tokens, occasionally up to ~4k in rare workflows.
- Streaming is required for the agent UI (progressive output matter to UX).

Immediate asks / what we will run
1) Perf matrix: run qualification against three input buckets (3k, 6k, 10k) crossed with three output sizes (512, 2k, 4k) and concurrency sweep [1,10,40,100]. Measure p50/p95/p99 for both time-to-first-token and full-response completion.
2) Streaming vs non-streaming comparison: validate time-to-first-token improvements with our SSE streaming path and quantify extra tail latency on long outputs.
3) Hedging strategy options: test fallback to a smaller quantized model vs progressive truncation + contextual summarization so we can surface trade-offs (latency, cost, and quality).
4) Canary plan: if baseline looks good, propose a 10% canary with traffic shaping and automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant under pressure.

Attachments: aurora_sample_prompts.txt (sample prompt set you provided), demo-recording.mp4 (call recording).

Proposed timeline
- Redwood runs qualification job Wed night (Nov 11). Results by Thu morning (Nov 12).
- Internal review + canary plan Thur afternoon; canary earliest Fri (Nov 13) if green.

Next steps for you
- Confirm the 10k worst-case input frequency (how often in a typical month) and whether those uploads can be routed to batch-processing instead of interactive sessions.
- Share any hard procurement / security gates we should know when we propose a dedicated pool for the canary.

I'll assign the qualification run to Laura; Rishi will own the canary rollout.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Sales Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
From: Alex Nguyen <alex@auroraanalytics.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO window sizing & streaming hedges — post-demo alignment

Thanks Soojin — that captures it cleanly. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 10k input is rare (roughly 2–3% of requests) but it happens during our nightly ingestion and some analyst uploads. Ideally we'd keep interactive flows <6k and route heavy uploads to batch, but we need the option to support 10k in emergencies.
- Cost / model choice: can you include rough delta estimates between the streaming-optimized model and the quantized fallback? We need to evaluate the unit economics before committing to a canary.
- Timeframe: Wed night for the run works for us. If you find any regressions in quality when truncating or quantizing, flag immediately — we have an internal QA team that can triage.

Also cc'd procurement@auroraanalytics.com in case vendor paperwork moves faster once we validate perf.

Alex Nguyen
Head of Product — Aurora Analytics
alex@auroraanalytics.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@auroraanalytics.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO window sizing & streaming hedges — post-demo alignment

Alex / team — plan for the perf qualification and the quick canary write-up below. I'm scheduling the job for Wed night (US-PST) as requested.

Qualification matrix (automation job)
- Input token buckets: 3k, 6k, 10k (use synthetic prompts from aurora_sample_prompts.txt).
- Output token targets: 512, 2k, 4k.
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 10, 40, 100. Sustained throughput target during each run: 120 req/s where applicable; we will simulate burst phases (400 req/s for 30s) to observe shedding behavior.
- Models to test: rdx-stream-1 (streaming-optimized), rdx-quant-6b (quantized fallback), rdx-base-13b (standard).
- Metrics captured: time-to-first-token (p50/p95/p99), full-completion latency (p50/p95/p99), token throughput, GPU utilization, and quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE proxy + manual QA spot checks).

Fallback strategies to evaluate
1) Route to rdx-stream-1 for interactive streaming; on degradation (p95 breach) fallback to rdx-quant-6b.
2) Progressive truncation with summarization: attempt prefix compression to keep input <=6k then complete on rdx-base-13b.
3) Preemptive batching for 10k uploads: route to async batch queue with separate SLAs.

Canary proposal
- Canary cohort: 10% of interactive traffic, 24h ramp with traffic shaping.
- Health gates: p95 latency <= 250 ms for non-streaming; time-to-first-token p50 < 150 ms for streaming; error rate <0.5%.
- If any gate fails, auto-fallback to rdx-quant-6b and alert on-call.

Deliverables & owners
- Perf results + spreadsheet (Laura) — Thu 11/12 09:00 PST
- Canary runbook + rollback checklist (Rishi) — Thu 11/12 13:00 PST
- Procurement packet + security questionnaire (Sojourn) — Soojin to coordinate with procurement thread.

Related links: HubSpot deal + Drive folder included in my submission. I'll post the job logs and perf graphs to the Drive link once ready.

-L

Laura Bennett

Acknowledged — thanks team. I'll finalize the canary runbook after Laura posts the perf spreadsheet. Two quick asks before we start: 
1) Procurement: please confirm any EULA or data residency notes we should include for dedicated capacity (procurement@auroraanalytics.com).
2) Quality guardrails: Soojin, please make sure the QA spot checks include 10 sample cases with the 10k input so we can evaluate truncation artifacts.

If both items look green by EOD Thu we'll target a Fri canary.
